spec.name: Yamlbase (Dogbase — agent-oriented local DB with Git-backed JSON storage)

nodes.title: Give agents a fast, queryable local DB whose data stays human-auditable and Git-trackable
Keep the SQLite index disposable and rebuildable from canonical JSON with a single command
The system is an agent-oriented local DB cache with deterministic file sync, not a 'JSON database' or 'ORM'
A constrained document-store CLI keeps agent data access safer and more evolvable than raw SQL
Per-record JSON localizes Git conflicts where monolithic JSONL is merge-hot
Derived-index architecture

detail.definition: JSON files are the source of truth; SQLite is a derived, disposable index. If SQLite and JSON disagree, JSON wins; if the index breaks, rebuild it.

nodes.title: Canonical JSON record

detail.definition: One per-record file at data/<collection>/<id>.json, checked into Git, that is the authoritative state for a record.

nodes.title: Document-store CLI

detail.definition: A small stable command surface (get/put/del/list/query) presented to agents that hides SQLite, migrations, indexing, and export machinery.

nodes.title: Drift

detail.definition: A discrepancy between the canonical JSON files and the SQLite index, surfaced by the status command and repaired by rebuild.

nodes.title: No off-the-shelf product combines a document-store CLI, SQLite query performance, and per-record JSON Git storage
PocketBase proves a single command auto-running migrations at startup is practical UX
Agents interact via get/put/del/list/query; no raw SQL exposed by default
Write path validates input, writes canonical JSON atomically, then updates the SQLite index (JSON-first)
The .db file is gitignored and fully rebuildable from canonical JSON via rebuild
Deterministic serialization: stable key ordering, normalized whitespace, atomic temp-file + rename writes
The status command reports drift between JSON files and the SQLite index
Collections, fields, and indexes are defined in config; the Drizzle schema derives from config
A single-writer file lock prevents concurrent CLI invocations from corrupting state
better-sqlite3's prebuilt binary works across macOS/Linux without native compilation issues
Per-record JSON performs acceptably in Git repos up to ~10k records per collection
Atomic temp-file + rename writes prevent partial or corrupt JSON on crash
Local-only: no remote sync, replication, or multi-machine writers
No raw SQL exposure by default; direct SQL is an opt-in escape hatch at most
No automatic Git operations; dogbase writes files and the user/agent commits them
If SQLite and JSON disagree, JSON wins; SQLite is always a derived index
Reads go SQLite-first (auto-rebuild if dirty); writes go JSON-first
Adopt the derived-index architecture

detail.chosen_option: JSON files are canonical; SQLite is a derived, disposable index rebuilt from JSON
rejected: SQLite-first: write SQLite then export to JSON
Treat Git itself as the database/query engine
detail.rationale: Keeping JSON authoritative preserves a human-auditable Git trail while SQLite supplies indexed reads; an inverted authority would corrupt the audit story.

nodes.title: Use Drizzle + better-sqlite3 over Prisma

detail.rationale: Drizzle is more headless and CLI-composable with clean folder-based migrations; Prisma pulls toward 'ORM app architecture' which is the wrong fit for a thin custom CLI.

nodes.title: Build a TypeScript CLI rather than a single Bash script

detail.chosen_option: TypeScript CLI (tsx in dev, compiled JS to ship), Bash only as a thin bootstrap shim
detail.rationale: Config parsing, schema-aware validation, deterministic import/export, and structured agent output make Bash brittle and hard to test.

nodes.title: Ship an npm-installed Node CLI rather than a single self-contained binary

detail.chosen_option: Standard bin entry in package.json; npm-installed Node CLI
detail.rationale: better-sqlite3 is a native module, so standalone cross-platform binaries are painful; npm install handles native compatibility conventionally.

nodes.title: Store per-record JSON files rather than monolithic JSONL

detail.chosen_option: One JSON file per record at data/<collection>/<id>.json
rejected: A single monolithic JSONL file per collection as canonical state
detail.rationale: JSONL creates a hot file every write touches — merge-conflict hell; per-record JSON localizes conflicts and yields per-entity reviewable diffs.

nodes.title: Use db pull / db push as the JSON-to-SQLite sync command names

detail.chosen_option: db pull imports canonical JSON into SQLite; db push exports records back to JSON
detail.rationale: Early design framed sync as pull/push to mirror familiar VCS verbs.

nodes.title: Rename sync commands to import / export instead of pull / push

detail.chosen_option: import / export command names for JSON-to-SQLite sync
detail.rationale: pull/push sounds remote; this is a local tool, so import/export better signals the local-only file-sync semantics.

nodes.title: Do not adopt Dolt at the data layer; use Git-backed JSON + disposable SQLite

detail.chosen_option: Git-tracked per-record JSON as canonical storage with a disposable SQLite index
rejected: Embedded/served Dolt as the version-controlled storage engine (as in steveyegge/beads)
detail.rationale: Dolt's cell-level MVCC and SQL-level commit history are powerful but heavyweight for a single-user local tool; branch/merge data semantics stay out of scope, revisited only if needed.

nodes.title: Git diffs of data/ are clean — no spurious changes from serialization instability
rebuild reconstructs SQLite entirely from canonical JSON — the DB is disposable
Concurrent CLI invocations are safely locked — no corruption under concurrent access
A monolithic JSONL hot-file merge conflict that per-record JSON avoids
A kill-during-write crash that atomic temp-file + rename must survive
Serializer golden tests: given known objects, assert exact deterministic JSON output
Round-trip test: serialize → parse → serialize yields identical output
Drift tests: deleting or adding a JSON file makes status report drift
Concurrent-invocation stress test: two CLI calls cannot corrupt state
Round-trip integration: put via CLI → verify JSON file → rebuild SQLite → query → assert identical record
doctor command validates schema, round-trip stability, foreign keys, and export determinism
beads/Dolt assessment: six version-control capabilities a plain SQL database cannot provide
Every slice must pass inner- and middle-loop tests before it is considered done
serializer.ts — deterministic JSON (stable keys, normalized whitespace, UTF-8)
json-store.ts — atomic, deterministic per-record file reads/writes
config.ts — load and validate config with zod
schema.ts — Drizzle schema and collection definitions generated from config
sqlite-index.ts — open SQLite (WAL, foreign keys, busy timeout, STRICT), run migrations, index ops
sync.ts — rebuild, reindex, and drift detection
lock.ts — single-writer file lock
Agent-facing command surface: init/get/put/del/list/query/import/export/rebuild/status/doctor
config.yaml: collection, field, type, nullable, indexed, and primary-key definitions
M1 — Walking skeleton and pure core modules
M2 — Derived-index sync, CLI surface, and integrity safety
Deterministic canonical storage (serializer + JSON store)
Schema-driven SQLite index (config/schema + migrations)

Frontier 5: SQLite index + migrations — pragmas, auto-migrate, CRUD via Drizzle
Frontier 6: Sync engine — rebuild from JSON and detect drift
Frontier 7: CLI commands — wire core modules into the command surface
Frontier 8: File lock — single-writer safety
Frontier 9: Doctor command — validate the whole system's integrity
